title: A record has every column its kind requires
statement: A record MUST have a value of the right type for each required column of its kind's table, and no column its table lacks.

title: A flow step fulfills only its own use case's requirements
statement: A flow step MUST fulfill only UC requirements of the use case its flow belongs to.

title: What is one stays one
statement: A use case MUST have at most one flow per interface; a constraint, invariant, specification, policy and flow at most one test; a pattern rule at most one test per domain; a design record at most one technical record, and an entity or read model at most one table; a policy MUST hear exactly one event; a flow step MUST invoke at most one command or query and happen in at most one view.

title: A command's recorded exception is another aggregate of its domain
statement: A command change MUST name an aggregate of the command's domain other than the command's own, with its reason.

title: An aggregate has at most one root
statement: An aggregate MUST NOT have more than one entity whose role is root. One with none is work still to do.

title: An entity has one table at most, in its root's or its own
statement: An entity MUST have at most one table, which holds rows of its own: never a `view` or a `materialized view`. A child stored in its root's table MUST NOT have a table of its own, and only a child MAY be.

title: A table's keys fit together
statement: A table MUST have at most one primary key, and a foreign key MUST point at a table of its own domain. A table kept in `browser storage`, a `file` or `in memory` MUST have no keys, and no foreign key MUST point at one. Only a unique key MAY name an invariant or a condition, and exactly a foreign key names its target table.

title: A field has exactly one type
statement: A field MUST be typed by exactly one of a basic type, a value object or an aggregate, and a value object's field MUST NOT be typed by its own value object.

title: A field's name is unique in its owner
statement: No two fields of one entity, value object, event or read model MAY have the same name, compared trimmed and in any letter case.

title: Each capability of a domain has its own position
statement: No two capabilities in one domain MAY have the same position. Capabilities in different domains MAY.

title: A flow's paths are numbered 1, 2, 3
statement: The steps on each path of a flow MUST each have their own position, and SHOULD run 1, 2, 3 without a gap. Steps on different paths MAY share a position.

title: A pattern rule's settings are its pattern's
statement: The setting a pattern rule depends on, and its applies-when setting, MUST be settings of its pattern, and an applies-when condition MUST be given whole or not at all.

title: An automated test's file names its test
statement: An automated test's file MUST exist and MUST contain the test's ID. A technical record's file MAY not exist yet: that shows as not built, not as breakage.

title: A product's kind is its own and never widens Lathe's
statement: A product kind MUST be declared once, by a name no Lathe table has, under a kind that exists, and its records MUST sit in the product that declares it. A product MUST NOT widen Lathe's kinds with another parent or more required columns.

title: A product relation adds a table or a pair, never changes Lathe's
statement: A product relation with a new name MUST get a link table of its own; one with Lathe's name MAY only add a pair its link table's ends accept and MUST NOT change Lathe's role, labels or description. Each pair is declared once, and every relation MUST have both its labels.

title: A product's declarations are described
statement: Every product kind, kind field and product relation MUST have a description, so the reference never shows a blank.

title: Parts stay inside their aggregate
statement: A `has_one` or `has_many` link MUST join two entities of one aggregate.

title: A domain is named for a capability, not a technology
statement: A domain SHOULD be named for what it does for someone. A title or domain code that holds a technology word as a whole word (web app, frontend, backend, API, UI, server, database, desktop, mobile, engine, infrastructure, Electron and the like) SHOULD be reported as a warning; the description is not read.

title: An event is named in the past tense
statement: A domain event's title SHOULD say what happened, subject first and in the past tense. A title with no past form as its last word or after its first SHOULD be reported as a warning.

title: Every child entity is reached from its root
statement: Each child entity SHOULD be reached from its aggregate's root by `has_one` or `has_many` links inside the aggregate. One that is not SHOULD be a warning, and an aggregate without exactly one root MUST NOT have its children judged.

title: A record with no owner is used
statement: A view, integration, value object, specification or UI component that nothing uses MUST be reported as an error.

title: A pattern rule test's domain follows its pattern
statement: A pattern rule test MUST name a domain that follows the rule's pattern, or has a use case that does.

title: An event a policy hears is delivered by outbox
statement: An event a policy hears SHOULD have an event type delivered by `outbox`, since a lost reaction is a lost change; one that is not SHOULD be a warning. An event that only keeps read models current (fed_by), where those read models are rebuilt from the data on every load, MAY be delivered `in process`.

title: A test runs at a level its kind allows
statement: A test's run by level SHOULD be one its kind allows; one that isn't SHOULD be a warning.

title: A write is all or nothing
statement: A write's commands MUST all take effect or none: when one is refused, the data and every data file stay as they were.

title: A write is checked whole before any file changes
statement: Each write MUST build the new state in one transaction, with every key, constraint and validation query of the schema, and MUST rewrite a data file only after the whole state passes.

title: A write rewrites only its tables' files, in one fixed form
statement: A write MUST rewrite only the data files of the tables it changed, each through a temporary file and a rename, rows sorted by key and columns in the table's order, so the same data always gives the same file and a changed row is a one-line diff.

title: Writes run one after another
statement: Writes to one store MUST run one at a time, each on the state the one before it left, so two writers never lose each other's change.

title: A refusal names every problem and where it is
statement: A refused write or load MUST name every problem it found, each with its rule, a message naming the table, row and value, and the data file and line of a loaded row or the index of the command that brought it.

title: A record changes parent only by a move, which carries what sits inside
statement: `set` MUST NOT change a row's key or a record's parent columns. `move` MUST give the record its new parent's column and clear the other, and the records inside it keep their parents and take the new scope.

title: A removal takes its parts and links, and is refused while referenced
statement: Removing a record MUST take its part rows and the links it starts, and MUST be refused, naming up to 20 referrers, while anything else still references it.

title: One name across Lathe's checks and every product's
statement: A check's name MUST be one key across Lathe's checks and every product's, so each problem's check name says whether Lathe or the product reported it. A product check named like one of Lathe's MUST be refused, naming `lathe/data/check.jsonl`.

title: Lathe's checks are read-only
statement: Lathe's own check rows, in `lathe/data/check.jsonl`, MUST NOT change or be removed by any write to a product: they are loaded beside its data as read-only rows.

title: A check documents itself
statement: Every check row, Lathe's or a product's, MUST give a one-sentence summary, an explanation ending with how to fix what it reports, its severity and its query, none of them empty.

title: A check's query is one SELECT that says what it returns
statement: A check's query MUST be a single `SELECT` (or `WITH`) statement returning `record` and `message`, and it MUST return `severity` exactly when the check's severity is `error_or_warning`.

title: A product has at most one settings row
statement: A product MUST have at most one `product_setting` row.

title: Every page has its own address
statement: Every page MUST have its own address that can be bookmarked, shared and reloaded, and the browser's back and forward buttons MUST move between pages.

title: Every pane shows the page's one focus
statement: The wiki pane, the graph pane and the side bar MUST always show the same record or group: the one the address names. Moving the center in the graph MUST change the address, and changing the address MUST move every pane.

title: A page shows the views it offers, the link's first
statement: When an address names views (`?view=wiki`, `?view=wiki,graph`, `?view=graph,model`) the page MUST open with those views, and they become the remembered ones; only an address without views MUST fall back to the views last open. A view the page does not offer (Model, away from a domain, aggregate or entity) MUST be dropped from what it shows; when that leaves none, the page MUST show the wiki.

title: A space's last page lasts the session
statement: The last page visited in each space MUST be remembered for the browser session only, never across sessions.

title: What is folded in the nav lasts the session
statement: Which nav rows are open MUST be remembered for the session only, never across sessions.

title: One tab per page at most, and one preview tab at most
statement: A tab group MUST NOT hold two tabs for one page, nor more than one preview tab. Opening a page already open activates its tab; a plain open of another page replaces the preview tab's page, keeping its place in the row.

title: There is always a tab
statement: A tab group showing a page MUST hold at least one tab, the page's. Closing its last tab MUST leave that page open, as the preview tab.

title: A tab's state is its own
statement: Changing the views, pane sizes or scroll of the active tab MUST NOT change any other tab's. A new tab copies the active tab's state when it opens, then goes its own way. How the graph is drawn is not a tab's state (LA-EXP-INV09).

title: Moving through the graph never changes how it is drawn
statement: The graph settings MUST be one for the browser session, whatever the tab or page. Opening, activating or closing a tab, an arrow step, a click or Enter on a box, a link, and Back or Forward MUST NOT change them; only the Change the graph settings command does.

title: A key binding means one command wherever it applies
statement: No two commands MAY share a binding in contexts that can be active at the same time, and no two-key sequence MAY start with a key that is a binding of its own.

title: Every theme has a light set and a dark set
statement: Every theme MUST set the core colors (shell, paper, sheet, ink, muted, rule, the accent and its tint, spark and its tint, and warning) in both its light and dark sets. Core colors a file leaves out are taken from Lathe; the other colors follow a core one or serve both modes unless the theme sets them.

title: Built-in themes are never changed
statement: A built-in theme MUST NOT be edited, renamed or deleted; it is changed by editing a copy. Reset puts a copy back to the built-in it was copied from, keeping its name.

title: The chosen theme always exists
statement: When the chosen theme no longer exists (deleted, or its stored data no longer reads), Lathe MUST be shown and chosen.

title: Each folder has one window
statement: No two product windows MAY show the same folder, however its path is spelled; opening a folder that has a window brings that window forward.

title: A server the shell starts never listens on 5199
statement: Every server the shell starts MUST listen on a free local port other than 5199, the Owner's own dev server, which the shell may only share (SP02).

title: Recent folders are listed latest first, each once, at most 10
statement: The recent folders MUST list the folder opened last first, each folder once (opening one again moves it to the top), and at most 10, dropping the oldest.

title: A setting value gives a value or a reason
statement: A setting value MUST give either a value or a not-applicable reason, never both and never neither, and a reason MUST NOT be empty.

title: Each followed pattern's settings take their own values
statement: A follower that follows two patterns with a setting of the same name MUST give each pattern its own value: a setting value names its pattern, and one pattern's value MUST NOT answer the other's.

title: A setting value answers a setting of a pattern its follower follows
statement: A setting value MUST name a setting its pattern has, for a pattern its follower follows.

title: A follower answers every setting of its pattern
statement: A domain or use case that follows a pattern MUST give each of the pattern's settings a setting value, a value or a not-applicable reason. The pattern's rules then apply to it with those values, and it does not restate them.
